title: Google: Email sender guidelines
supports: Senders to Gmail need SPF or DKIM; senders of more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail accounts need SPF, DKIM and DMARC, must support one-click unsubscribe for marketing and subscribed messages with List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers, and must keep the Postmaster Tools spam rate below 0.10% and avoid ever reaching 0.30%
limit: Page mentions Feb 1, 2024 and Dec 2023 start dates and no later revision date; thresholds and enforcement have changed before, so read the live page; it does not state an unsubscribe deadline, and a small sender below 5,000 a day is not held to the bulk rules but should still follow them

title: Yahoo Sender Hub: sender requirements and best practices
supports: Bulk senders implement SPF and DKIM and publish a DMARC policy of at least p=none that passes, keep spam rate below 0.3%, implement a list-unsubscribe header with one-click unsubscribe for marketing and subscribed messages (RFC 8058 POST highly recommended), and honour unsubscribes within 2 days
limit: Page says enforcement began in February 2024 and was rolled out gradually; it carries no revision date; the definition of a bulk sender and spam-rate basis sit elsewhere on Yahoo's site and were not read

title: FTC: CAN-SPAM Act compliance guide for business
supports: Commercial email needs accurate header information, a subject line that reflects the content, a clear disclosure that it is an advertisement, a valid physical postal address, a clear explanation of how to opt out, opt-outs honoured within 10 business days, and you cannot contract away responsibility for compliance; each violating email can bring penalties of up to $53,088
limit: United States law only and the penalty figure is inflation-adjusted, so confirm the current amount; it does not require prior consent, unlike the UK and EU rules

title: ICO: How do we comply with the PECR electronic mail marketing rules?
supports: UK rules for marketing email to individuals: consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous, with no pre-ticked boxes, silence or inactivity; consent is not transferable and must be easy to withdraw; the products and services soft opt-in has five listed conditions; every message must offer a simple, free opt-out
limit: UK law (PECR with UK GDPR), not EU member-state law or other regimes, though EU GDPR is similar in its consent definition; the page shows a 5 February 2026 date for the new charity rule and no other revision date; this is regulator guidance, not legal advice

title: Product Hunt Launch Guide: how Product Hunt works

title: Product Hunt Launch Guide: preparing for launch

title: Product Hunt Launch Guide: sharing your launch

title: YouTube Help: how views are counted
supports: From August 24, 2026 a view is counted the moment a video starts to play, across Shorts, long-form videos and live streams; YouTube checks that views come from real people, which takes time, and counts can change after publication or be slowed, frozen or adjusted; Realtime shows only estimates
limit: Page describes counting and validation in general terms and gives no delay in hours or days for final numbers; older data may use a different view definition, so compare periods carefully

title: YouTube Help: check your impressions and watch time
supports: Thumbnail impressions are how many times thumbnails were shown to viewers on YouTube; an impression counts when the thumbnail is on screen for more than one second with at least half visible; impressions click-through rate is how often viewers watched a video after seeing the thumbnail
limit: A separate YouTube FAQ page, fetched, adds that impressions on external websites and end screens are not counted and views from other sources can make CTR differ from views divided by impressions; neither page gives a target CTR for a new channel

title: YouTube Help: determining if your content is made for kids
supports: Creators must designate whether content is made for kids and it is their legal responsibility to comply with COPPA and other laws; factors include whether children are the intended or actual audience, child actors or characters, and early-education or game content; mixed-audience content that targets children as one audience counts; general audience content (teens or older) should be set as not made for kids; made-for-kids videos are more likely to be recommended alongside other kids' videos
limit: Page is guidance, not legal advice, and no single factor decides; it does not itself list the feature restrictions, which sit on other YouTube Help pages not fetched here, so check them before relying on comments or other features for study-app audiences

title: YouTube Help: spam, deceptive practices and scams policy
supports: Titles, thumbnails and descriptions that trick users into clicking are prohibited; repetitive or deceptive comments and messages meant to drive traffic are spam; bots, coercion or rewards for likes, views or subscribers are prohibited while asking viewers to like, comment or subscribe is allowed; violations can bring removal, strikes or termination
limit: Fetched summary does not reproduce every example; enforcement judgments are YouTube's, and the page does not give thresholds

title: Reddit Help: how old do I need to be to use Reddit

title: Search Console Help: what are impressions, position, and clicks
supports: Impressions are counted when a link to your site appears, including below the fold when no click on see more is needed; clicks are counted when a user goes from Google to a page outside Google; CTR is clicks divided by impressions; position uses the topmost position per query then averages across queries, and is recorded only when the link got an impression
limit: Page explains the metrics but not how well they predict real use; average position is an average over queries and not a live rank

title: Search Console Help: Performance report (Search results), about the data
supports: The newest data is sometimes preliminary and may change within hours; by default only complete days are shown; chart totals are aggregated by property while tables aggregate by page, so impressions, CTR and average position differ between them; exports show dashes and tildes as zeros
limit: Fetched text did not cover data retention or anonymized queries; a search extract mentions an impressions logging error from May 2025 to April 2026 on a data-anomalies page that was not fetched

title: Google Search Central: spam policies for Google web search
supports: Lists spam categories including cloaking, doorway abuse, keyword stuffing, link spam, scaled content abuse, site reputation abuse and thin affiliation; scaled content abuse is generating many pages mainly to manipulate rankings rather than help users; violating sites may rank lower or not appear, via automated systems or manual action

title: Google Search Central: SEO starter guide
